title: The five integrated elements and how they fit together
blurb: Name the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 7, say what each one is and show how they fit together.
question: Which integrated element of PRINCE2 7 influences how the principles, practices and processes are applied by the people involved, so the method fits the project?

teach.body: PRINCE2 7 is built from five integrated elements: principles, people, practices, processes and the project context. The principles are the foundation. People, practices and processes are built on them. All of it sits inside the project context, which shapes how the method is applied. Plain English: rules you must follow, the humans who make it work, the topics you manage all the way through, the steps you take, and the setting you work in.

teach.caption: The principles underpin everything; the project context surrounds everything.

teach.body: PRINCE2 7 puts people at the centre of the method. Understanding the needs, capabilities and motivations of those involved, and the relationships between them, is crucial to how the project is set up and run. The element covers both the people working on the project and the people affected by it.

Practices are aspects of project management (business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues, progress) that must be addressed consistently and continually as the project runs; each explains the treatment needed for the processes to work. Processes are the seven sets of activities that take the project from before it starts to its closure, with checklists of recommended activities and responsibilities.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Orchard Lane Schools Trust
teach.body: Orchard Lane Schools Trust is replacing the pupil records system in nine schools. Project manager Daniel Achterberg checks all five elements. Principles: all seven will be applied. People: teachers and office staff affected by the change are engaged early. Practices: risk and quality are managed throughout. Processes: the project moves from starting up to closing. Project context: a public-sector trust, data protection rules and a supplier working iteratively.

teach.text: Practices are NOT processes. Practices (such as risk or progress) are aspects addressed continually; processes (such as controlling a stage) are sets of activities in the lifecycle. And 'themes' and 'four elements' are 6th edition terms: PRINCE2 7 has five elements and seven practices.

items: Five integrated elements: principles, people, practices, processes, project context (1.2).
Principles are the foundation; if they are not applied, it is not a PRINCE2 project.
People sit at the centre and include those working on and affected by the project.
Practices are addressed continually; processes run from pre-project to closure.
The project context surrounds everything: organizational and commercial context, delivery method, sustainability requirements and scale.

summary: You can now name the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 7 and explain what each one is. You can also describe how they fit together, with principles as the foundation and everything inside the project context.

A.q: Which is one of the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 7?
options: Themes
People
Tolerances
Stages
A.why: The five integrated elements are principles, people, practices, processes and the project context (1.2).

whyNot.0: Themes is the 6th edition term; PRINCE2 7 calls them practices.
whyNot.2: Tolerances are part of manage by exception and the progress practice, not an integrated element.
whyNot.3: Stages are how a project is divided for management, not an integrated element.

A.q: Which integrated element describes the whole lifecycle, from activities before the project starts to its closure, with checklists of recommended activities?
options: Practices
Principles
Processes
Project context
A.why: The seven processes describe the project lifecycle from pre-project activities through to closure, each with checklists of recommended activities and responsibilities.

whyNot.0: Practices are aspects of project management addressed continually, not the lifecycle of activities.
whyNot.1: Principles are guiding obligations, not a lifecycle of activities.
whyNot.3: The project context is the setting the method must fit, not a set of activities.

A.q: Which integrated element consists of guiding obligations and good practices that decide whether a project is genuinely managed using PRINCE2?
options: Practices
Processes
People
Principles
A.why: The seven principles are guiding obligations and good practices; unless they are applied, it is not a PRINCE2 project.

whyNot.0: Practices describe aspects of project management to address continually; they do not define whether a project is PRINCE2.
whyNot.1: Processes are the activities through the lifecycle, not the test of whether a project is PRINCE2.
whyNot.2: People concerns the needs, capabilities and relationships of those involved, not the defining obligations.

B.q: Which integrated element describes aspects of project management that must be applied consistently and continually throughout the project lifecycle?
options: Practices
Processes
Principles
People
B.why: The seven practices are aspects of project management that must be addressed consistently and throughout the lifecycle.

whyNot.1: Processes are sets of activities at points in the lifecycle, not continually addressed aspects.
whyNot.2: Principles are the guiding obligations underpinning the method.
whyNot.3: People concerns those involved and affected, and their relationships.

B.q: Identify the missing words in the following sentence. The [?] element reflects that PRINCE2 is designed to work in any organizational or commercial setting, delivery method, set of sustainability requirements and scale.
options: principles
practices
project context
tailoring
B.why: The project context element: PRINCE2 can work within any context, and the people involved apply the principles, practices and processes so the method fits.

whyNot.0: The principles underpin the method; the element describing the setting is the project context.
whyNot.1: The practices are aspects of management; they do not describe the setting.
whyNot.3: Tailoring is how the method is adapted, but it is not one of the five elements; the element is the project context.

B.q:
Which two statements about the integrated elements are correct?
1. The principles form the foundation for the other elements.
2. The people element covers just the people working on the project.
3. PRINCE2 7 has five integrated elements, up from four.
4. The practices are the seven processes followed in sequence.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Principles are the foundation (statement 1), and PRINCE2 7 has five elements where the 6th edition had four (statement 3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: the people element covers those working on the project and those affected by it.
whyNot.2: Statements 2 and 4 are false: people includes those affected, and practices are not processes.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: practices are aspects addressed continually; processes are a separate element.

C.q: Which element covers understanding the needs, capabilities and motivations of those involved, and where does it sit in the PRINCE2 7 model?
options: Principles; as the foundation beneath the others
People; at the centre, resting on the principles
People; as the outer layer around the others
Project context; at the centre of the others
C.why: People are at the centre of the method, alongside practices and processes and resting on the principles; the project context surrounds them all.

whyNot.0: Principles are the foundation, but they are guiding obligations, not about people's needs and motivations.
whyNot.2: The people element is central; the outer layer around everything is the project context.
whyNot.3: The project context surrounds the method; it is not the element about people's needs and motivations.

C.q: Which element forms the foundation of PRINCE2, and what follows if it is not applied?
options: Processes; the next stage cannot be authorized
Practices; the project loses its business case
Principles; the project is not a PRINCE2 project
People; the project board must be replaced
C.why: The principles are the foundation; unless they are applied, the project is not genuinely being managed using PRINCE2.

whyNot.0: Processes are built on the principles; they are not the foundation.
whyNot.1: Practices are built on the principles; the business case is one practice, not the foundation.
whyNot.3: People are at the centre, not the foundation, and PRINCE2 sets no such rule.

C.q: A public-sector trust works under strict data rules, uses a supplier with its own iterative method and runs a mid-sized project. Which element describes these factors, and how does PRINCE2 deal with them?
options: Project context; the people involved apply the method to fit
Principles; the project board rewrites them to fit the trust
Practices; the supplier's method takes the place of them
Processes; the business layer approves a new process set
C.why: Organizational context, delivery method and scale are part of the project context; the principles, practices and processes are applied by the people involved so the method fits.

whyNot.1: Principles are not rewritten or tailored away; they apply to every PRINCE2 project.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 governs a supplier's iterative method; the practices still apply.
whyNot.3: PRINCE2 does not replace its processes with a new set; they are tailored to the context.

reteach.title: Think of a restaurant kitchen
reteach.question: A kitchen has house rules, a team, standards it maintains all the time, a sequence of service steps and a particular venue. How do these map to the five elements?

blocks.body: The house rules every dish must follow (hygiene, freshness) are the principles: break them and it is not this restaurant's food. The chefs and front-of-house staff are the people. The standards watched all service long, such as stock, cost and quality, are the practices. The steps from prep to plating to clearing down are the processes. Whether it is a beach café or a hotel banquet is the project context, which shapes how everything is done.

blocks.text: Standards watched all the time (practices) are different from the steps taken in order (processes).

explain.body: Seven guiding obligations and good practices. They are the foundation of the method; unless all are applied, the project is not a PRINCE2 project.

test.q: How many PRINCE2 principles are there, and how many must be applied for a project to be PRINCE2?
options: Seven, and all of them must be applied
Seven, and at least five must be applied
Five, and all of them must be applied
Six, and each one may be tailored away
test.why: There are seven principles, and all of them must be applied for a project to be a PRINCE2 project.

whyNot.1: There is no partial threshold: all seven principles must be applied.
whyNot.2: Five is the number of integrated elements, not principles.
whyNot.3: There are seven principles, and principles are not tailored away.

explain.body: Covers the needs, capabilities and motivations of everyone involved, and the relationships between them. It includes those working on the project and those affected by it. People are at the centre of PRINCE2 7.

test.q: Whom does the people element of PRINCE2 7 cover?
options: The project board and the project manager
The team members and the supplier's staff
Those working on and affected by the project
The users who will operate the products
test.why: The people element covers both those working on the project and those affected by it.

whyNot.0: The board and project manager are included, but the element is wider: everyone working on or affected by the project.
whyNot.1: Team members and supplier staff are included, but so are the people affected by the project.
whyNot.3: Users are included, but the element also covers everyone working on the project and others affected.

explain.body: Practices: seven aspects of project management addressed continually (business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues, progress). Processes: seven sets of activities from starting up to closing a project.

test.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes practices from processes?
options: Practices are steps in sequence; processes are aspects managed throughout
Practices are aspects managed throughout; processes are activities in the lifecycle
Practices are set by the business layer; processes are set by the project board
Practices apply to the delivery stages; processes apply to the initiation stage
test.why: Practices are aspects of project management addressed continually; processes are the sets of activities that run through the lifecycle.

whyNot.0: This swaps the two: practices are addressed continually, processes are the activities.
whyNot.2: Neither is set by the business layer or board; both are part of the method, tailored to the project.
whyNot.3: Both practices and processes apply across the whole lifecycle, not one kind of stage.

explain.body: PRINCE2 is designed to work within any context: organizational and commercial context, delivery method, sustainability requirements and project scale. The people involved apply the principles, practices and processes so the method fits.

Example
rows: Public trust with an external supplier

test.q: Which of these is a factor within the project context element?
options: The number of principles applied
The format of the project log
The delivery method being used
The order of the seven processes
test.why: The project context includes organizational and commercial context, delivery method, sustainability requirements and project scale.

whyNot.0: All seven principles are applied in every context; their number is not a context factor.
whyNot.1: The project log's format may be tailored, but it is a management product, not a context factor.
whyNot.3: The processes are part of the method; their use is shaped by the context, not a factor of it.
